title: Solstice Retail - Procurement & Onboarding: MSA/DPA Exceptions Review
summary: Kickoff to align on MSA and DPA exceptions, data residency and KMS requirements, and pricing path for a pilot. Redwood AE/SE walked through exception asks; customer raised concerns around auditability, key management, and minimums. Agreed next steps: send redline DPA/MSA notes, provide SOC2 and architecture diagram, schedule technical benchmark pilot in non-prod VPC.
topics: KMS/HSM integration and Bring Your Own Key (BYOK)
next_steps: Redwood to send redline summary for MSA/DPA by 2025-09-11
Redwood to share SOC2 Type II report and architecture diagram (private plane) by 2025-09-12
Schedule SE-led technical benchmark pilot (30-60 min) for week of 9/22/2025
Customer to confirm list of PII scopes and legal approver by 9/15/2025
action_items: Lena Park (Redwood) - prepare DPA redline summary PDF and a one-page exceptions matrix - due 2025-09-11
Marco Diaz (Redwood) - produce pilot runbook and architecture diagram for VPC deployment (include KV cache notes) - due 2025-09-12
Priya Singh (Solstice) - confirm compliance contacts and which datasets are in scope for pilot - due 2025-09-15
Tom Reynolds (Solstice) - provide procurement timeline and any required PO process details - due 2025-09-16
transcript:
Meeting header: 2025-09-09 15:00 PT / Duration ~52 minutes. Attendees: Lena Park (Redwood AE), Marco Diaz (Redwood SE), Priya Singh (Head of Platform, Solstice), Tom Reynolds (Procurement), Aisha Omar (InfoSec), Ben Cole (Legal joined 00:12).

[00:00] Lena: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. Quick roll call - yep, I'm Lena from Redwood, Marco is here to handle the technical bits. Aaron might pop on later.
[00:08] Priya: Hi Lena, thanks. Priya here. We sent over the MSA and DPA earlier, Tom and Aisha are here to go through exceptions.
[00:15] Tom: morning all, yeah procurement side - want to clarify SLAs and minimums before we go deep.
[00:22] Marco: great, I'll do a quick overview of the deployment options because I know Aisha cares about the KMS and private VPC stuff.
[00:30] Aisha: yep, thanks. We'll need proof of encryption at rest with customer-managed keys and an audit trail. Also, retention controls — we can't persist PII beyond 90 days.
[00:40] Lena: Understood. On the MSA, the two main asks we saw were indemnity cap adjustments and a data processing addendum exception around pipeline logs. Can you run us through the specific DPA lines that are blocking you?
[00:54] Priya: The log retention clause is the big one. We also want clarity on subprocessor notification windows, like 30 days notice rather than the broad language.
[01:05] Ben: (joins late) Sorry for delay, Ben from legal. We'd like to limit liability for infra failures that we don't control and add SOC 2 references.
[01:15] Lena: Totally reasonable. For SOC 2 we can share our latest report. For liability we usually push for mutual indemnity with carve outs for third-party cloud providers.
[01:28] Marco: On the technical side, we can support BYOK via KMS integration and HSM-backed keys if needed. You'll need a dedicated private deployment or a VPC private control plane for that, which changes pricing vs hosted.
[01:42] Tom: Pricing is the other question. What's the delta between hosted and private? And are there minimum commitment levels?
[01:50] Lena: There are a few levers — hosted has lowest onboarding friction and per-token pricing; dedicated capacity (Reserved) gives you predictable throughput and isolation for a monthly commit. Private deployments (VPC or on-prem) incur platform fees and will require a 6-12 month commit typically. We can run numbers after the pilot.
[02:08] Aisha: We also need egress controls, data locality in AWS eu-west-1 for our EU customers, and audit logs forwarded to our SIEM.
[02:18] Marco: We can route requests by region and pin model variants. Audit logs can be shipped to your S3 or Splunk via push. Quick note: KV cache was mentioned in your doc — that's just internal cache keys, we can redact/disable prefix caching for sensitive workloads.
[02:36] Priya: When you say redact, do you mean you could disable caching for specific routes?
[02:41] Marco: yes, route-level controls. You pick which model routes have caching, batching parameters, etc. That reduces per-token cost but if you need no cache we can turn it off.
[02:52] Tom: back to MSA indemnity, our counsel wants a $5M cap for IP infringement and a separate cap for general liability. Is that negotiable?
[03:03] Lena: We'll need to take that to legal — our baseline is tied to fees paid in the last 12 months, but for enterprise deals we usually accept higher caps with commercial terms like higher commitment or insurance.
[03:16] Ben: Also need clarity on subprocessor list and a process for DPA amendments. If a new subprocessor is added, 30 days notice and an opt-out path is required.
[03:26] Lena: We can add a notification window, though opt-out might mean pause of data or designated migration window. We'll capture the ask and propose language.
[03:36] Priya: For the pilot we want to test 3 model endpoints against our existing in-house inference to compare latency and quality. Can you run a benchmark in our dev VPC?
[03:47] Marco: Yes, we can spin up a non-prod VPC and run a 24-48 hour benchmark. Need sample payloads and an SSH key exchange or service account with scoped permissions. We'll provide a runbook.
[03:59] Aisha: For the benchmark environment, don't store logs in Redwood long-term. We need retention set to 7 days and logs exported to our Splunk instance.
[04:10] Marco: Noted. We'll set retention policies and provide an export mechanism.
[04:16] Tom: How about SLA credits? Our ops team expects >=99.9% for production and clearly defined remedies.
[04:24] Lena: Our dedicated offering has 99.9% with credit schedules; hosted is best-effort with SLOs but not identical crediting. For enterprise we can discuss SLA attachments to the MSA.
[04:36] Priya: Any red flags about compliance? We do process PII and payment metadata for orders. Need to confirm PCI boundary assumptions too.
[04:45] Marco: We don't handle PCI directly unless you route tokens through a tokenizer or redaction step. We can document the in/out dataflow and propose a PCI isolation approach.
[04:56] Priya: ok good. Also, are there export controls or country-of-origin issues if the model weights are hosted in us-east-1?
[05:04] Lena: We support region pinning. For export control language, we'll run legal on that but we can commit to region residency on data and inference requests. We should note model artifacts are often replicated; if that is an issue, a private deployment may be required.
[05:19] Ben: On liability, what about subcontractor flowdowns — we need to ensure obligations pass to subprocessors.
[05:25] Lena: Standard flowdown language is possible; we can propose a template.
[05:30] Tom: timeline question — we need procurement sign-off by end of October to hit our Q4 roadmap. Is that realistic?
[05:36] Lena: If we can get a pilot in September and have the DPA/MSA redlines closed by mid-October, that's feasible. Hence the next steps we outlined.
[05:45] Marco: I'll follow up with a technical checklist: sample payloads, VPC peering steps, IAM role template, and a small config YAML for model params (batch size, kv cache on/off, token limits).
[05:58] Priya: one more thing — data deletion proof. We need a revocation workflow so legal can show data was deleted after the pilot.
[06:06] Marco: We have deletion APIs and can produce a signed deletion receipt plus keys to demonstrate zeroed data. We'll include that in the runbook.
[06:15] Lena: Great. Recap: Redwood will send a concise redline and exceptions matrix, SOC2 and architecture diagram, and a pilot runbook. Solstice will confirm datasets and procurement timeline. We'll schedule the pilot week of 9/22. Any last items?
[06:30] Priya: not from me. Thanks.
[06:33] Tom: I'll loop procurement in and get PO path details to Lena.
[06:36] Ben: expect a follow-up email with legal points from my side within 48 hours.
[06:40] Lena: Thanks everyone. We'll follow up in email and book the pilot slot.

End of transcript.

Notes about transcript quality: sporadic timestamps captured; occasional mis-heard acronyms (KV cache recorded as K V cash in earlier auto-transcription), some speaker labels generic or delayed when Ben joined.
